steps.text: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium-high heat; cook the onion in the hot oil until tender, about 5 minutes. Add the ground beef, bell peppers, tomatoes, tomato sauce, tomato paste, and red pepper flakes to the saucepan; stir.
Reduce heat to medium-low; simmer until peppers are soft and beef is tender, 4 to 6 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Dynamites
raw_recipe.description: This Dynamites recipe is for loose-meat sandwiches popular in Rhode Island. They feature green bell peppers and onion with canned tomato sauce, tomato paste, and diced tomatoes.
raw_recipe.name: Dynamites

review.reviewBody: I searched for a Dynamites recipe to surprise my husband, who is from Rhode Island. When I found this one, it looked easy enough for an amateur like me to try. It was - easy and fantastic! Thanks!

Just returned from vacation with a wicked cold, and I’ve now lost my taste, so this review is from my husband. I had no green bell peppers, so I used red and yellow (on hand) and served on a bakery hamburger bun. Cooking for 4-6 hours seemed like a long time, but I was at home anyway and ended up cooking stove top for 3 hours. And this well may be the time that you pull out the slow cooker, just makes sense. I will say that the meat really tenderized (yeah, ground beef can be chewy/tough), so if not the full amount of time listed, do give it enough time simmering. He really liked the consistency of the meat, asked me to dial back the red pepper flakes in the future (personal taste), and felt it needed more seasoning. I added salt, pepper, garlic powder, and some Worcestershire. Basically, he liked this sandwich and said he’d like to have it again.

Kicked up Sloppy Joe's. Love it. The four bell peppers are a stroke of genius. I thought it was too much, but they broke down beautifully. I always go nuts with these kinds of recipes. I put in jalapenos and chopped cilantro, too. When I took my first bite I screamed DYN-O-MITE! I felt like JJ Evans from Good Times.

A whole lot like the "sloppy joes" I grew up eating in the midwest during the 1950s. They often showed up in the school cafeteria. Due to the drip factor, I've never cooked them--plain burgers and hot dogs can be messy enough. I expect DH and my kids would have enjoyed them, but I didn't want to hand wash tomato stains out of their clothes and would have needed a drop cloth in the dining room. The cooking time seems excessive--my mom rarely cooked this melange for more than an hour, and the ground beef was pretty melty and the tomatoes collapsed into a delicious sauce in that time. I did look up my mother's recipe--1 lb lean gr beef, 1 onion, 1 green bell pepper, 1 quart of home canned tomatoes, lightly chopped, 1 can tomato paste--very close!

I’m from Rhode Island but have lived in California for the past 25 years. I often get cravings for hot wieners, doughboys, pizza strips, stuffies, and all those other amazing Rhode Island favorites. My mom used to make Dynamites— but she called them Torpedoes and served them on grinder rolls— and we LOVED them. I happened upon this recipe and realized, this is her torpedo recipe! I made them following the recipe exactly except I added a few dashes of Frank’s Red Hot for a little zing. I cooked it in a crock pot for about 4 hours. I served them open-faced on grinder rolls and they were absolutely delicious! Tasted just like mom’s torpedoes!

I’m a native Woonsocket-er as well. Do NOT put celery in these. It will only make it more watery. And instead of dicing the onions and peppers, slice them. Also, use red peppers instead of green. It makes the dynamites a little sweeter.
My family loved the Dynamites. I did add 1 tsp. of garlic powder, 1/2 tsp. of salt and 1/4 tsp. of pepper. I left out the green pepper because grandkids do no like the green pepper.
We call these sloppy Joe's. But I use the Manwich canned sloppy Joe sauce. I top mine with onions and pickles.

I personally like celery in my dynamites so I add that, and season my hamburger with salt pepper and garlic powder. Other than that this is a great recipe. Made it several times, serve dynamites on a hoagie bun with a side of potato or pasta salad and chips. Good stuff

3 1 17 ... http://allrecipes.com/recipe/186860/dynamites/ ... Hadn't heard of Dynamites till now. 'Reminds me of sloppy joe's or "Manwhich" (but much better tasting). I added a half t salt. Upping the red pepper would've been fine. It isn't spicy, just tastes good. Should I have drained the meat? I was feelin' reckless & the recipe didn't say I should. Well, I did what I could with that orange oil. I will drain next time or mostly drain. Thanks for the recipe! A couple days later, I pressed boy, 19, for a review & got at thumbs-up. Fair enough. ;D
I put cut up chunks of pepperoni in mine! Gives it the spicy dynamite “kick” I’m from RI also! 😋
I’m born and raised in RI and this sandwich has been a RI staple for generations. It’s kinda like a ramped up sloppy Joe, type sandwich, with a lil kick, or a lot…a whichever you prefer
Added Cajun seasoning to taste Omitted peppers
This was pretty bland in my opinion. Made exactly as the recipe said. That was seriously so much waiting for a dinner that was mediocre.
I didn't think it had much flavor. I put bread and butter pickles on my sandwich which helped a little.
These are another version of Sloppy Joes! Really nothing new! 🤷

My family all grew up in RI and they called this "torpedo meat" since it was served on torpedo rolls. A&W Restaurants served it in the 70's. My mother made this often and was always a family favorite.
